research_question: Does independent literature overturn the nuisance-only conclusion that Commodity should keep the current volatility line on HOLD?
search_scope: Independent post-feasibility triangulation using peer-reviewed natural-gas volatility mechanism, structural-change, and event-jump research not used in the pre-feasibility snapshot. No protected Commodity confirmation outcomes were inspected.

sources.title: What drives volatility in natural gas prices?
Inventory announcements, jump dynamics, volatility and trading volume in U.S. energy futures markets
A hybrid econometrics and machine learning based modeling of realized volatility of natural gas

claim_map.claim: Natural-gas volatility is structurally time-varying and materially linked to supply- and demand-side shocks, supporting mechanism-aware rather than invariant all-history designs.
Inventory announcements are associated with jump and volatility behavior in energy futures, supporting event-specific designs only when the event population is defined ex ante.

HAR remains a useful natural-gas realized-volatility benchmark and nonlinear models can matter in some volatility regimes, but this does not justify adaptive model shopping without adequate information.

expected_observations: Independent literature should support volatility persistence and mechanism/event heterogeneity without implying that a nearby horizon or more complex model automatically creates independent information.
A future material redesign may be credible if an ex-ante mechanism changes the event population or information structure enough to reduce nuisance variance or increase effective information.
disconfirming_observations: Independent evidence shows that simply changing the forecast model or nearby horizon reliably overcomes the programme's measured information deficit.
A literature-supported mechanism can be converted into a fresh confirmation without a new nuisance-only power calculation or independent confirmation allocation.
